subject: filtering for custom range allele frequency

messages.author: 9433ca4167c39272
messages.subject: filtering for custom range allele frequency
parts:
Hi, 

I've been trying to find a way to filter for allele frequencies that are above the 0.5 threshold that is set in the gl.filter.maf code. 
I tried to extract this info from the gl.report.maf function because of the maf.limit command but it doesn't seem to change anything and I can't get an output from the report other than the plot (which doesn't go below nor beyond 0.5, no matter what limit I set). 
I'm sure there is a way to get this from somewhere, right? And to custom set ranges of allele frequencies to subset?
In particular, I'd like to only look at alleles with a frequency of 0.4-0.6.
is there a way to custom set the range in gl.filter.maf or to extract that info through gl.report.maf (so I could then create a new subset including only those loci)?

Also, congratulations to the new beta update, some of the new functions look exciting!

Thanks and merry Christmas,

Katrin

messages.author: be5831679f44e5dc
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] filtering for custom range allele frequency
parts:
Hi Katrin,

The .5 limit would be because if it is more than .5, it’s no longer the minor allele, it’s the major allele. So if you set a MAF of .4 and above, I think you get what you want.

Cheers,

Renee

messages.author: be5831679f44e5dc
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] filtering for custom range allele frequency
parts:
Hi Katrin,

If the minor allele frequency has to be .4 and above, then the major allele frequency has to be .6 and below, because they add up to 1 for every locus. So just filtering on a maf of .4 should give you what you want.

Cheers,

Renee

Hi Renee, 

I figured that above 0.5 is major, however, there is no filter for major allele frequencies. I can easily just filter maf >0.4 but I need to figure out how to filter <0.6 :-)
But thanks for your answer.
